shots.loi: Could James Harden step back so far that he actually traveled through time?
In 2019, Harden averaged
36 .1 points per game,
largely thanks to one of the most unguardable
step backs in NBA history.
But what if he stepped back a little too far?
Houston,
tie game, five
seconds left.
Harden crosses over his defender and takes one step back. Suddenly, it's 1996.
Michael Jordan is now guarding him.
Jordan gets into his defensive stance. Harden
immediately steps back again. 1891,
James Naismith is still inventing basketball.
Harden asks where the three -point line is.
Naismith asks what a three -pointer is.
Harden keeps dribbling.
One more step back sends him to ancient Rome, 44 BC. Three
Roman legionnaires form a defensive wall.
Harden pump fakes.
The entire formation jumps.
He tries to draw a shooting foul. The
Romans have absolutely no idea what
he's complaining about. Eventually,
a Roman official blows his whistle. Traveling,
Harden immediately demands a replay review.
Unfortunately, cameras won't be invented for
another 2 ,000 years.
Final stat line, zero points, zero assists, and over 2 ,000 years of traveling.
